figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Heterologous expression and production of ODL derivative NOSO-95A (1) in E. coli. (A) A bioinformatics study was conducted to identify
native ODL producers and to determine the gene borders of ODL biosynthetic genes using BLAST, HHpred and various alignment and dotplot
tools. The ODL BGC was designed for heterologous expression in E. coli. The BGC was divided into nine gene fragments with unique restriction
sites at the 3’ and 5’ ends, compatible with the adjacent gene fragment, respectively, to allow assembly of the cluster on the pNOSO expression
plasmid using restriction/ligation techniques. Created with BioRender.com. (B) The ODL BGC consists of four NRPS genes, odlS1-4, (green) and
eight putative tailoring genes, odlA-H, (colored) predicted to be responsible for compound modifications. The BGC is under the control of the
T7lac promoter system (brown). A kanamycin resistance gene cassette (orange) was chosen for the selection of the correct clones, and the origin
of replication (ori) is the p15A ori (grey). Schematic representation of OdlS1-4, module (M) indications and the corresponding domain legend in
the box below. A domain specificities are shown inside the schematic A domains and were derived from the ODL sequence described by Pantel
et al. 2018.[3] K=lysine, Dab-OH=3-hydroxy-2,4-diaminobutyric acid, G=glycine, O=ornithine, P=proline, H=histidine, K-OH=δ-hydroxy lysine,
Dha=Z-dehydroarginine. The generated expression plasmids carrying ODL BGC, verified by sequencing, were transformed into E. coli BL21 (DE3)
and fermented under different culture conditions. (C) The concentrated culture was analyzed by HPLC/MS techniques. The production of 1 in trace
amounts was validated using a standard 1 as a control. (D) Structure of NOSO-95A (1) and theoretical residues (R1 and R2 of NOSO-95 derivatives
A, B and C).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. (A) Schematic representation of the cross-feeding experiment with NRPS-1 and OdlB. (B) HPLC/MS data of compounds 3 and 7
produced in E. coli DH10B::mtaA expressing NRPS-1 with odlB in a cross-feeding experiment. Straight line (j) indicates two different strains with a
different set of plasmids co-cultivated in the same flask. Depicted are EIC’s of compound 9 (m/z [M+H]+ =399.29) and 12 (m/z [M
+2H]2+ =322.24). EIC signal intensity corresponding to production culture of E. coli DH10B::mtaA expressing NRPS-1 and odlB is 15 times
decreased compared to all other signals. (C) HPLC/MS (HILIC) data of E. coli DH10B::mtaA expressing odlB under the depicted conditions. EICs
of compound 15 (m/z [M+H]+ =119.08) and 16 (m/z [M+H]+ =135.07).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. (A) Schematic representation of NRPS-2 with color code of the original NRPS. A domain specificities are indicated with Q=glutamine,
Dab-OH=3-hydroxy-2,4-diaminobutyric acid and L=leucine. HPLC/MS base peak chromatograms (BPC) of compounds 17 to 20 produced in
E. coli DH10B::mtaA expressing NRPS-2 with or without co-expression of odlB. Chemical structures with respective peptide origin highlighted in the
color of the original NRPS domains. (B) Schematic representation of NRPS-3, -4 and -5. A domain specificities are indicated with K=lysine,
Q=glutamine, T=threonine and L=leucine. HPLC/MS data of compounds 22a, 22b, 26a, 26b, 33a, 37b and 38 produced in E. coli DH10B::
mtaA expressing NRPS-3, -4 or -5 with or without co-expression of odlG with 24 hours delay. Depicted are EIC’s of compound 22a and 22b (m/z
[M+H]+ =422.36), 26a and 26b (m/z [M+H]+ =442.32) and 33a and 33b (m/z [M+H]+ =331.22), 37a and 37b (m/z [M+H]+ =242.18) and
38 (m/z [M+H]+ =260.19). Peptide/amino acid building blocks are highlighted in the color of the original NRPS domains.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. (A) Schematic representation of NRPS-6 with color code of the originated NRPS and the biosynthesis mechanism involving OdlF and
OdlE. Product structures with respective peptide origin are highlighted in the color of the corresponding BGC. A domain specificities are indicated
with Q=glutamine, A=alanine, R-OH=β-hydroxy L-arginine and K-OH=δ-hydroxy lysine. (B) HPLC/MS data of compounds 39 to 42 produced in
E. coli DH10B::mtaA expressing NRPS-6 with odlF or odlEF. EIC’s of compound 39 (m/z [M+2H]2+ =355.74), 40 (m/z [M+2H]2+ =390.79), 41
(m/z [M+2H]2+ =363.74) and 42 (m/z [M+H]+ =708.47) are shown. Furthermore, a cross-feeding experiment is included where a straight line
(j) indicates two different strains with different sets of plasmids co-cultivated in the same medium. (C) Schematic representation of NRPS-7 and its
product formation of either 47 or 48 with and without co-expression of odlF. (D) Table of NRPS-6 variants and NRPS-8 with their ability to produce
compound 39 and 40 when co-expressed with odlF.
